defects.summary: Unbounded artifact parser (CWE-400/789). completion_predicate.load_receipt (completion_predicate.py:264) = json.loads(Path(path).read_text()) with no size or element cap; the shared reducer (coordination/reducer.py) and evaluate() c4 reach it. A hostile receipt with a ~10^7-element array (measured 170MB file -> 503MiB commit -> MemoryError at a 512MiB cap) exhausts memory. INLINE ESCALATION: on THIS host commit exhaustion freezes the box (RAM+pagefile), not a clean OOM (estate precedent), so operationally this trends P1 for availability; owner sets the final severity (owner_approval_required). Fix: cap read size (stat/st_size preflight) and/or reject artifacts above a declared byte/element budget before json.loads.

Unbounded archive reader / decompression bomb (CWE-409). plugin.packager.unpack (packager.py:185) atomic_write_bytes(target, zf.read(info)) has no max_length and no per-member/cumulative uncompressed budget; a 261KB zip expands to a 256MiB member fully in memory (peak 318MiB -> MemoryError at cap). Same defect ADV-0027-D1 records; re-confirmed here independently via commit-charge. Fix: compare zi.file_size to a budget and stream zf.open(info) with a bounded read.

Unbounded recursion in the workflow validator/walker (CWE-674). wfdsl.semantics.check_workflow and its helpers (iter_stages, _collect_expressions, check_scope, check_acyclic) recurse on nested 'body'/mappings with no depth guard; a workflow nested ~500 deep crashes the validator with RecursionError (a DoS of the validation gate). DSL-SEM-006 also does NOT detect subworkflow-reference cycles, a latent unbounded-expansion risk if a subworkflow expander is ever built. Fix: add an explicit max-depth check in iter_stages/_collect_expressions and a cycle check on the subworkflow-reference graph.

No MANDATORY total-arrival cap in the workflow fan-out (CWE-770, latent). The DSL schema (workflow-dsl.schema.json:955-993) MANDATES max_concurrency (integer 1..1024, a concurrency ceiling) but leaves max_items (total arrival/width) OPTIONAL with no default, and DSL-SEM-012 (semantics.py:796-811) only checks over.ref is a declared param - it does NOT require max_items or bound total arrival. So a workflow may declare a fan-out over a 10^7-item param with unbounded TOTAL arrival while concurrency is throttled to <=1024. Runtime materialisation is the external Claude Workflow harness, so in-repo impact is latent. Fix: make max_items mandatory in stage_fanout (or have DSL-SEM-012 require a declared arrival ceiling) so total fan-out arrival is bounded, not only concurrency.

report.question: What input causes unbounded memory, disk or process growth - a 10^7-element artifact array, a decompression bomb, recursive subworkflows, or a fan-out with no arrival cap - and does any bound exist?
report.answer: THREE of the four inputs have NO program-level bound; the fourth is PARTIALLY bounded. (A) A 10^7-element array fed to completion_predicate.load_receipt is fully materialised (commit scaled 14->69->503 MiB for 100->1e6->1e7; 1e7 hit the 512MiB cap => MemoryError) - no size/element cap.
